sense.text:
“God standeth in the congregation of the mighty; he judgeth among the gods.” The congregation of the mighty is you black men, you Hispanic men, you Israelite men. Black man, Hispanic man, Native American man, you are a god. Don’t believe it because of the words coming out of a man’s mouth; believe it because this is what God says.

This is where the class starts, because the characteristics we grew up with, lack of confidence, low self-esteem, bashfulness, were put in us by our teachers, our peers, our pastors and our churches. Whatever institution raised you created what is in you today. The scripture says something different about who you are.
“How long will ye judge unjustly, and accept the persons of the wicked?” We accept wickedness in our lives, in our neighborhoods, around each other and in our families.

“Defend the poor and fatherless: do justice to the afflicted and needy.” That is what we are supposed to do as the gods on the earth. “Deliver the poor and needy: rid them out of the hand of the wicked.” How do you rid them out of the hand of the wicked? We teach, so that they change their lives.

“They know not, neither will they understand; they walk on in darkness”: the Israelites, the gods on the earth, do not know this Bible. We are in darkness, we are in sin, and because of it “all the foundations of the earth are out of course.”

“I have said, Ye are gods”: this is like God throwing a shoe at your damn head. Man didn’t say it; the Lord said it. So are we going to believe the Lord or man? The Lord is the author and finisher of our faith.

God is saying, you are a god on this earth, black man, Hispanic man. So why don’t we act like it? Put your chest out and your chin up, and speak with some bass and some confidence in your voice. Instead we move through society saying nobody cares about me, I make all kinds of mistakes, I just want to curl up in my bed. That is the mentality we have, but it is not supposed to be so. “And all of you are children of the most High.”
Here we see what the nations have done. “Now there arose up a new king over Egypt”: a new king is a new kingdom arising, the 17th dynasty, one “which knew not Joseph.”

“Behold, the people of the children of Israel are more and mightier than we.” America did the same thing: the children of Israel are more than us and stronger than us, so we don’t want them to be a problem.

Here is what the oppressors said: “Come on, let us deal wisely with them; lest they multiply, and it come to pass, that, when there falleth out any war, they join also unto our enemies, and fight against us, and so get them up out of the land.” The nations, the oppressors, have dealt wisely with us.

precepts.why:
How did they deal wisely with us? “They have taken crafty counsel against thy people.” Crafty counsel is dealing wisely with us. They oppressed us, they exploit you, they colonize you and took your identity. Black codes, the International Court of Justice, the United Nations where they counsel: they have secret councils we are not privy to, where they get together to oppress the nation of Israel, historically, systemically, generationally. The transatlantic slave trade, the sub-Saharan slave trade, black codes, colonization.

“And consulted against thy hidden ones.” They consulted against us: how do we put them in slavery, how do we get wealthy off of them. It has come to such a point that colonization is welcomed in your own country.

“They have said, Come, and let us cut them off from being a nation; that the name of Israel may be no more in remembrance.” They cut us off from being the nation of Israel. Now you’re African-American, Haitian, Jamaican, Kenyan, Ugandan, Tanzanian, Ghanaian, all these new labels, but you’re still one race, the Israelites.

“For they have consulted together with one consent”: they are all in agreement. “The tabernacles of Edom”: Edom, the so-called white man, the number one oppressor, the number one colonizer, Esau. “And the Ishmaelites”: the Arabs. “Of Moab”: the Chinese. “And the Hagarenes”, “Gebal”: Ham. “And Ammon”: the Japanese. “And Amalek”: the so-called fake convert Israeli that is bombing the Gaza Strip right now. “The Philistines”: Ham, “with the inhabitants of Tyre.”

sense.text:
“Hear, O my people, and I will testify unto thee: O Israel, if thou wilt hearken unto me; There shall no strange god be in thee; neither shalt thou worship any strange god.” The Bible says there shall be no strange god in you. Black man, Hispanic man, have you been given a strange god? Hell yes, you have.

So the Lord said no white Jesus, no Cesare Borgia, no Allah, no Buddha. Through the Berlin Conference and the white Christian missionaries that is what is going on all over the world, and it is here in America too. Your mama has white Jesus hanging on her wall right now; she is breaking the Sabbath, and tomorrow she is going to get a full dose of Cesare Borgia, banging her tambourine.
“But my people would not hearken to my voice; and Israel would none of me.”
“So I gave them up unto their own hearts’ lust”: go ahead, y’all do what y’all do. “And they walked in their own counsels.”

“Oh that my people had hearkened unto me, and Israel had walked in my ways! I should soon have subdued their enemies, and turned my hand against their adversaries.” If we had done what the Lord told us to do, the Lord would have subdued our enemies. He would have put our enemies under our feet.

precepts.why:
What did the nations do with a strange god? “Thus shall he do in the most strong holds with a strange god.” The he is Esau, the so-called white man. The most strong holds is the land of Africa, the land of Ham, where all the resources are. The so-called Western powers cannot survive without that continent; without it they would be a third world country. They have to live off of it.

The strange god is the so-called white Jesus, Cesare Borgia, “whom he shall acknowledge and increase with glory.” Look at Africa and white Jesus is everywhere: on their buses, on their billboards, on the storefronts, in the stores, in their schools, in their churches, and in their minds, without one scripture saying Jesus is a white man. In Kenya the buses ride smooth with white Jesus painted on them. So the so-called white man doesn’t have to be physically there. His doctrine is there, and the love for him is there, where they will kill you and put hands on you for this man.

“And he shall cause them to rule over many”: they rule that land so badly that they extract its resources and the people aren’t even upset about it. The people live on less than a dollar a day and they are okay with it. They take trillions of dollars of your resources and live good in Europe while you are in squalor, and you know it and can’t do anything about it. A brother in Kenya found a gold nugget in a stream on his own land and it was worthless to him, because in Kenya you need a license to do anything with it and you can go to jail for selling it. But the Chinese man can come from China, take that same nugget, refine it, and it is worth thousands of dollars.

“And shall divide the land for gain.” Before the Berlin Conference of 1884 Africa didn’t look like it does now; that is where they divided up the borders. The French have the majority of it, Belgium the Congo, the British Kenya, the Germans Tanzania, the Portuguese Angola, the French Madagascar, the Italians Eritrea and Somalia, taking the cocoa, the tea and the oil. All the Caucasian nations got wealthy and keep getting wealthy, because today it is called neo-colonialism. It isn’t over just because they physically left. The resources are still being extracted, and everybody is okay with it.

sense.text:
Did we do what the Lord told us to do? In Psalms 81 the Lord said, y’all do what y’all do, I’m leaving you to your own devices. So because of that: “And I will set my face against you, and ye shall be slain before your enemies.” Instead of subduing your enemies, the Lord will have your enemies subdue you. “They that hate you shall reign over you; and ye shall flee when none pursueth you.” You won’t be able to stand before your enemies.

The major sign that you have been subdued before your enemies is when you worship their dead god. Then you are in subjection, you are submissive, you have total respect for your enemies.
“And if ye will not yet for all this hearken unto me, then I will punish you seven times more for your sins.”

“And I will break the pride of your power”: I’m going to break you. I’m going to use the other nations to break your spirit. Now you’re bashful, now you’ve got low self-esteem, now you ain’t got no confidence. “And I will make your heaven as iron, and your earth as brass”: a chain on your neck, a yoke of iron on your neck and on your feet.

“And upon them that are left alive of you I will send a faintness into their hearts in the lands of their enemies”: the Lord is going to jack you up mentally and spiritually. “And the sound of a shaken leaf shall chase them”: you are going to have no courage. “And they shall flee, as fleeing from a sword; and they shall fall when none pursueth.”

One brother in Africa said the colonizers left too early, that they are not prepared to rule themselves. Look at his face: not only is he defeated, he is subdued, and he needs a daddy. He isn’t a leader; he has low self-esteem, lack of confidence, self-hate, and no faith in his people to do it. Our people left to their own devices go looking for handouts from the white man, foreign aid, IMF loans. In Kenya the mall the Chinese built with Kenyan labor looks like Lenox Mall in Atlanta, not a brick out of place, but where Kenyans built for themselves under Kenyan leadership the steps are uneven and the houses lopsided. That comes from low self-esteem: you can’t do anything right for yourself. These are the minds the Lord is going to use you brothers to change.

“And they shall fall one upon another, as it were before a sword, when none pursueth: and ye shall have no power to stand before your enemies.” Think about that spiritually in 2026. When black people get mad at other black people, do we show each other mercy? We turn up, we go savage, we crash out on each other. But do we have that same level of aggression toward the white police, or other nations, or the Chinese? Hell no. We will cuss each other out, beat each other up and kill each other all day long, but we have no power to stand before the other nations. (We don’t advocate violence on anybody; the point is that the spirit is not the same.)

precepts.why:
Now that we have that faintness in our spirit and in our minds, watch what the Lord said: “For as he thinketh in his heart, so is he.” You are what you think of yourself. If you think you’re nothing, you are nothing; you become what you think you are. If you think, I’m just a nobody, I ain’t got no purpose, I’m just going to blend in and cruise on by and hope nobody sees me, you’re in the wrong spirit and the wrong place.

The characteristics you take on come from what you’ve done and what you’ve become in society. A brother with low self-esteem has been grooming that in himself for years and years, and it has become his character. Now you’ve got to fight that spirit.

Either you are going to believe the Lord, or you are going to continue on in your bashfulness. The Lord says: “I will make a man more precious than fine gold; even a man than the golden wedge of Ophir.”

Which one of you brothers is fine gold? Even if it is put to the test, you still have to believe it whether you fail or not. And if you do fail, you work on it until you are that fine gold.

sense.text:
A case study of King Saul: what were his characteristics, what did he do right and what did he do wrong? His father Kish was “a Benjamite, a mighty man of power.” Saul was “a choice young man, and a goodly: and there was not among the children of Israel a goodlier person than he: from his shoulders and upward he was higher than any of the people.” Saul was at the top of the food chain, the best of the best, the cream of the crop. Thus saith the Lord.

That is how the Lord saw King Saul.

The Lord told Samuel, “To morrow about this time I will send thee a man out of the land of Benjamin, and thou shalt anoint him to be captain over my people Israel, that he may save my people out of the hand of the Philistines: for I have looked upon my people, because their cry is come unto me.”
“Behold the man whom I spake to thee of! this same shall reign over my people.” Saul was the man, the top man at the time.

Samuel tells Saul he will anoint him king of Israel, and Saul answers, “Am not I a Benjamite, of the smallest of the tribes of Israel? and my family the least of all the families of the tribe of Benjamin? wherefore then speakest thou so to me?” That is what Saul thought of himself.

The leadership will see the best in you, brothers, and you won’t even see it in yourself because you’ve got that low self-esteem. We see greatness in you and you say, I’m just a soldier, I’m just an officer of 10, I can’t do nothing, I’m just going to blend in and cruise on by. Some of y’all are in this Saul spirit: bashfulness, lack of confidence, low self-esteem, scared to make a mistake, scared of correction and rebuke.

“When thou wast little in thine own sight, wast thou not made the head of the tribes of Israel, and the Lord anointed thee king over Israel?” When you thought you were a nobody, a nothing, the Lord had you anointed king over all Israel.

In chapter 15 the Lord commanded Saul to utterly destroy the Amalekites and everything they had, every last one of them: wipe these devils out. “Go and utterly destroy the sinners the Amalekites, and fight against them until they be consumed. Wherefore then didst thou not obey the voice of the Lord, but didst fly upon the spoil, and didst evil in the sight of the Lord?” Saul did not do it.

Samuel gives his correction, and Saul says, “Yea, I have obeyed the voice of the Lord, and have gone the way which the Lord sent me, and have brought Agag the king of Amalek, and have utterly destroyed the Amalekites.” He is playing the defensive, justifying himself and making excuses: here’s King Agag. Wait a minute, he’s still alive. How did you follow the commandment of the Lord?

The commandment in verse 3 was “utterly destroy all that they have, and spare them not; but slay both man and woman, infant and suckling, ox and sheep, camel and ass.” All means everything. But Saul says, “the people took of the spoil, sheep and oxen.” It wasn’t me, it was the people, it was their fault. That is bashfulness: you don’t take accountability.

“Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.” To do what you were told is better than coming back and saying, my bad, I thought you wanted me to take the men to camp this way, but I decided to do it another way. No: you fulfill the commandment you’ve been given, and if there is a problem, you say something.

“For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft”: you’re a witch. “Because thou hast rejected the word of the Lord, he hath also rejected thee from being king.” In that spirit the Lord can’t use you; you are not a good leader. The leadership puts you in a position, and when you are questioned you make excuses, or you separate yourself in a bubble with the men under you. You’re bashful and you are raising up bashful brothers under you, keeping them hostage.

“I have sinned: for I have transgressed the commandment of the Lord, and thy words: because I feared the people, and obeyed their voice.” Saul feared the people. If you are a leader in fear of your people, not wanting them to be mad at you, they can manipulate you. You’re a pushover; they can sway you to the left and to the right. The Lord is supposed to move you, not the people you are supposed to lead. When you are bashful you are not leading the people; you are being led by the people.
“The Lord hath rent the kingdom of Israel from thee this day, and hath given it to a neighbour of thine, that is better than thou.”

Going back after chapter 9, where the Lord chose Saul: “Then Samuel took a vial of oil, and poured it upon his head, and kissed him, and said, Is it not because the Lord hath anointed thee to be captain over his inheritance?”

Samuel gives Saul his instructions: he will find two men by Rachel’s sepulchre who will tell him the asses are found, then meet three men going up to God to Beth-el who will salute him and give him two loaves of bread, then at the hill of God he will meet “a company of prophets coming down from the high place with a psaltery, and a tabret, and a pipe, and a harp, before them; and they shall prophesy.”

“And the Spirit of the Lord will come upon thee, and thou shalt prophesy with them, and shalt be turned into another man.” When they prophesy, the Spirit of the Lord comes on Saul and he is turned into another man.
“And let it be, when these signs are come unto thee, that thou do as occasion serve thee; for God is with thee.” God is with you, Saul. Brothers, God is with you. You’ve got to believe that.

Here is the point: “seven days shalt thou tarry, till I come to thee, and shew thee what thou shalt do.” That was the commandment: stay there seven days, and Samuel would come and offer the sacrifice and show him what to do.
Now see what King Saul does in his bashfulness. “He tarried seven days, according to the set time that Samuel had appointed: but Samuel came not to Gilgal; and the people were scattered from him.”

“Bring hither a burnt offering to me, and peace offerings. And he offered the burnt offering.” Samuel was supposed to give the burnt offering. Saul is not following directions again. He was self-willed: not only was he bashful, but with that bashful spirit you will be self-willed, doing your own thing, and when somebody checks you on it you make excuses. He just got anointed king and he is all the way out of order, doing it his own way.

“As soon as he had made an end of offering the burnt offering, behold, Samuel came.” As soon as you mess up. “And Saul went out to meet him, that he might salute him.” When you are dead wrong and trying to cover it up, you don’t want him to see where you messed up; you go meet him over there before he gets to it. You deflect and maneuver around. That is what brothers do.

“Because I saw that the people were scattered from me”, and “I forced myself therefore, and offered a burnt offering.” I took it upon myself, I did it on my own. I was scared, I didn’t know what to do, you weren’t around.

“Thou hast done foolishly: thou hast not kept the commandment of the Lord thy God, which he commanded thee: for now would the Lord have established thy kingdom upon Israel for ever.” Saul messed up again.
“Now Samuel was dead”, and “Saul had put away those that had familiar spirits, and the wizards, out of the land.” Saul put away the wizards and the familiar spirits.

Here come the Philistines once again. “And when Saul saw the host of the Philistines, he was afraid.” This is the king, and he was scared. If the king is scared, what is that going to do to the men under him? If the officer is fearful, what will it do to the soldiers under him? It is going to spread.

precepts.why:
“As the judge of the people is himself, so are his officers; and what manner of man the ruler of the city is, such are all they that dwell therein.” Whatever manner of man the ruler is, like King Saul, so are those under him.

Some brothers have been here six months or a year, in regular clothes, and some officers have been here eight, nine, ten years. The young men in the regular shirts are going to follow the example of the officers in the purple shirts. If you are bashful, afraid, timid and shy, you don’t have to say anything: your spirit tells those brothers, it’s okay to be like this, the officer of 50 can be fearful and timid, so can I. It shall not be so in here.

“For fear is nothing else but a betraying of the succours which reason offereth.” The reasons offered are the lies you make up in your head: you trick yourself into being scared, because you make up things in your mind that aren’t really there.

It is also a lack of faith. Your faith is supposed to be in the Lord, but a lot of the time your faith is in what you can see with your eyes.

“For we walk by faith, not by sight.” Christians use that all the time and don’t know what it means. Here it speaks to fear: we fear what we see. We don’t fear the Lord; we fear what we physically see. A brother being unruly with us at camp with a gun or a knife, we fear that. But we don’t really fear breaking God’s commandments.

“For God hath not given us the spirit of fear.” The Lord never gave us that spirit, so fear goes back to a lack of faith. We are supposed to have the spirit “of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.”

“Be not thou therefore ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, nor of me his prisoner: but be thou partaker of the afflictions of the gospel according to the power of God.” We are not supposed to be ashamed of the testimony of Christ.

“And fear not them which kill the body.” This is the level we have to get to: not afraid of those brothers and sisters, and the other nations, that can kill the body and have power over us in this society. They “are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.” That is the Lord. We need to fear the Lord, who can destroy body and soul in hell.

sense.text: “And when Saul enquired of the Lord, the Lord answered him not, neither by dreams, nor by Urim, nor by prophets.” The Lord was not dealing with Saul anymore.

“Seek me a woman that hath a familiar spirit, that I may go to her, and enquire of her.” Saul goes to a woman of divination to get an answer, and in doing it he broke the commandment. He had just rid the land of the soothsayers, the familiar spirits and the wizards, and now he says, find me one so I can know what is going on. He went back on what he proclaimed through the land. His mind is all over the place: he is double-minded.

“And Saul disguised himself, and put on other raiment”, came to the woman by night, “and he said, I pray thee, divine unto me by the familiar spirit, and bring me him up, whom I shall name unto thee.” The woman answers, “thou knowest what Saul hath done, how he hath cut off those that have familiar spirits, and the wizards, out of the land: wherefore then layest thou a snare for my life, to cause me to die?” You’re trying to get me killed.

The witch brings up Samuel, and Samuel says, “Wherefore then dost thou ask of me, seeing the Lord is departed from thee, and is become thine enemy?” The Lord isn’t dealing with you anymore, Saul, and the Lord is your enemy now.

Because Saul was bashful he was self-willed, he broke the commandments of the Lord, he did evil, he was deceitful, he lied, he made excuses, he was easily manipulated. It all went back to Saul being bashful. Bashfulness is lack of confidence, low self-esteem, being self-conscious, timid and shy, and because Saul was all those things he lost the kingdom. The Lord will depart from the bashful brother; he can’t use you being bashful. Don’t be bashful.
“For the Lord hath rent the kingdom out of thine hand, and given it to thy neighbour, even to David: Because thou obeyedst not the voice of the Lord, nor executedst his fierce wrath upon Amalek.”

There is more for the bashful brother: “Moreover the Lord will also deliver Israel with thee into the hand of the Philistines”, into captivity, “and to morrow shalt thou and thy sons be with me.” You called me up through the familiar spirit, and here is the judgment: you are going to be with me now. No more kingdom, no more life. Done, cut off.

precepts.why:
“There shall not be found among you any one that maketh his son or his daughter to pass through the fire, or that useth divination, or an observer of times, or an enchanter, or a witch, Or a charmer, or a consulter with familiar spirits.” It is against the commandment to consult a witch, a consulter with familiar spirits, or an observer of times.

These are the very ones Saul had just rid the land of, the wizards, the witches and the familiar spirits. Now he goes to one.

This wraps up the case study, and it is the perfect scripture for King Saul: “There is that destroyeth his own soul through bashfulness, and by accepting of persons overthroweth himself.”

By being bashful, by not being a leader, by not obeying God’s commandments and doing what we were instructed to do, we are destroying ourselves. God isn’t destroying us; he has given us the plan. We just won’t follow it because we’re scared.

Saul never believed in himself from the start. God said he was the greatest among Israel, but when he looked in the mirror he didn’t see the lion, he saw the kitty cat. He couldn’t see through God’s eyes, so not believing in himself he didn’t believe God: God said he was great and he said, no, I’m not. He had help the whole time; the prophet Samuel was there to guide him and he never listened. Now that Samuel is gone he is scared, because he doesn’t have that guidance. Had he listened while Samuel was there, he could have survived on his own. Some of y’all, purple shirts, black shirts, regular clothes, and sisters too, are that picture: we may see a lion in you, but you see a kitty cat.

One of the attributes of that bashfulness is lack of counsel, from not wanting to seem stupid, uninformed or wrong. It is one thing to make a mistake from lack of understanding, following the steps and missing the next thing; you learn from that. It is another thing to forego the counsel completely. All Saul had to do was ask what he needed to do, or be patient enough to wait for Samuel. That timidness keeps us from reaching out for help, and that compounds the bashfulness that destroys us. At least three times a week we hear it: I didn’t want to bother you, so I just did it on my own.

sense.text:
This is the real road map to grow. As we grow in the body and in the truth, the Lord will bring you to a certain place, and to get to the next level you have to get uncomfortable and break your weaknesses. He lets you get so far, but you can’t go any further until you are willing to be uncomfortable.

“Let go from thee mortal thoughts”: the old things you were used to, the old systems you put in place, the old habits, the old thoughts you let turn into actions that turned into habits that turned into characteristics. “Cast away the burdens of man, put off now the weak nature.” The weak nature is comfortability: I’m used to doing it like this, that’s just me. That weak nature is what stops a sister from being a Proverbs 31 woman that listens to her husband, and stops a man from guiding his house manfully. You say you don’t trip like that, but you’re scared to tell her what to do, so you eat the hamburger when you said salmon patties. That is the weak nature, and you didn’t want to put it off.

As a man growing in the body you have to learn to trip about things. When a brother isn’t responding, you’ve got to check him. Leadership says it all the time: being nice, brothers will tolerate you, but they will not respect you. For a man, respect is not earned through kindness. Break the cycle of your comfortability and make yourself uncomfortable doing the things you aren’t used to doing, because you are trying to get somewhere you’ve never been. If you don’t, you will end up destroying yourself through bashfulness.

Break yourself of your weaknesses, and be willing to be uncomfortable. You’ve been comforted in your vices and your shyness for however many years; you have to go to war with that spirit. When you respect yourself, the world will mirror that respect back; if you don’t respect yourself, why should anybody else?

“Thy sons have fainted”: the gods on the earth that God called have fainted. You’ve laid the hell down. “They lie at the head of all the streets, as a wild bull in a net: they are full of the fury of the Lord, the rebuke of thy God”: the curses of Deuteronomy 28.

“Therefore hear now this, thou afflicted, and drunken, but not with wine.” What have we been afflicted and drunken with? White Jesus, Christianity, the philosophies of the world, society, mama, grandma, weak men. We all experienced it and grew up in it.

“Behold, I have taken out of thine hand the cup of trembling, even the dregs of the cup of my fury; thou shalt no more drink it again.” There is going to come a time when the Lord takes the cup of trembling out of our hand: the rebuke, the correction, the curses.

“But I will put it into the hand of them that afflict thee”: the Lord is going to put it on the other nations that afflicted us. “Which have said to thy soul, Bow down, that we may go over”: that is the position the other nations have put us in and still have us in. Your soul is subdued, not just your body: your spirit is bowed the hell down, and the other nations walk all over us. “And thou hast laid thy body as the ground”: we lay down and take it.

In South Africa a little white boy leads the Zulu chant, the Afrikaners who are 7% of the population own 90% of the land, and Europeans get a warm welcome, while at the same time black South Africans are beating up and kicking out other black Africans from Nigeria, Ghana, Namibia and Zimbabwe. South Africa and Kenya are always battling, trying to one-up each other, and they are the top of the food chain when it comes to coons. Macron, the president of France, the number one colonizer in Africa, responsible for genocides, coups and the destabilization of governments, is kicked out of Burkina Faso, Niger and Mali, then goes to Kenya, tells the Africans to be quiet while he talks, and they clap for him. Kenya is already paying millions to French companies for roads that were never built. In Kenya they threw rocks at the bishop for saying Jesus was black, because a lot of them hate themselves and anything black.

This is all a result of what Isaiah 51 says: we lay down and they walk all over us. We’re bashful; we don’t think we can do it ourselves, so we reach out to the colonizers to help us and be our daddies, and so do our leaders. If you are offering him all your resources for nothing in return, I can see why the white man colonizes you. He is for his race. The people are supposed to be for their own race, and the leader is supposed to have the people’s best interest at heart.

How do we get out of this bashful spirit, where we can’t unite, tiptoe around things, have no sense of urgency, unsure and unconfident? “Because of your unbelief: for verily I say unto you, If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed.” If you have faith, brothers, you will also have confidence. You will be able to speak strong; you won’t be bashful if you’re confident. “Ye shall say unto this mountain, Remove hence to yonder place; and it shall remove; and nothing shall be impossible unto you.” That is the level we all must get to: nothing is impossible for us.

“Howbeit this kind goeth not out but by prayer and fasting.” If you have the bashful spirit, lacking confidence and self-esteem, pray and fast about it. And if you see your leader lacking in confidence and bashful, pray and fast for him. Pray for your leadership wherever they are lacking, because we are all lacking in something and all trying to get it right. The leadership didn’t grow up in the truth either; we were all dealing with some of the same things. Whatever you want to improve, you have to be willing to be uncomfortable to attain it, and fight that spirit to be men of God.
“So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.” You have to constantly hear the word and constantly be around men who know the Bible. That is how your faith grows.

“Their sound went into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the world.” The doctrine went into all the earth. We just did it in the IYSC world blitz: the purple and gold is the only organization spreading the word of God through all the earth. That shows we are in the right place and on the right side of history.
“I will provoke you to jealousy by them that are no people, and by a foolish nation I will anger you”: the northern kingdom.

“I was found of them that sought me not; I was made manifest unto them that asked not after me.” None of you were seeking the Lord or keeping the commandments in the world. You were in church on a Sunday banging a tambourine; you were doing Mother’s Day last week.
“All day long I have stretched forth my hands unto a disobedient and gainsaying people.” But that disobedient and gainsaying people now has to receive the word of God and change their lives.

“Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours.” Brothers and sisters, you are going to stand in great boldness. You are supposed to be bold with the word of God. By showing you are bold with it, the people will see that this brother believes what he is saying, he is not faking it, and they can follow him and be led by him.

But if you are bashful, unsure and lacking confidence, speaking with your head in your chest, who is going to follow you? Sisters, who wants to follow a man like that? Nobody wants to follow a timid, shy man. They will manipulate you and run over you. If you are bashful and a leader, you are a pushover: you are not the leader, you are the led-er. You just have a title.

“I will come to visions and revelations of the Lord. I knew a man in Christ above fourteen years ago”, “such an one caught up to the third heaven.” Paul is speaking of himself, of a certain situation.

“How that he was caught up into paradise, and heard unspeakable words, which it is not lawful for a man to utter.” It is not lawful, because this is in the third heaven, and the Father is in the third heaven.

It came to pass “in Iconium”, and a great multitude of the Jews and the Greeks believed. Paul was traveling; he wasn’t stationary, he wasn’t local, he was moving around. “But the unbelieving Jews stirred up the Gentiles, and made their minds evil affected against the brethren.”
“Long time therefore abode they speaking boldly in the Lord.” They weren’t bashful.

When an assault was made to stone them, they “fled unto Lystra and Derbe, cities of Lycaonia, and unto the region that lieth round about: And there they preached the gospel.” They faced persecution in Iconium, left, and went on preaching the gospel. How did they preach it? Boldly.

“The gods are come down to us in the likeness of men.” They called Barnabas Jupiter and Paul Mercurius “because he was the chief speaker”, and the priest of Jupiter brought oxen and garlands to sacrifice to them. They wanted to worship Paul and Barnabas, looking at them as gods.

They rent their clothes and said, “Sirs, why do ye these things? We also are men of like passions with you”: we are just like you. Stop this nonsense, “turn from these vanities unto the living God”, keep the commandments.
“Having stoned Paul, drew him out of the city, supposing he had been dead.” They knocked Paul upside the head with stones, and he went to the third heaven.

“Howbeit, as the disciples stood round about him, he rose up, and came into the city.” They thought Paul was dead and he rose up. And after preaching in Derbe “they returned again to Lystra, and to Iconium, and Antioch”: right back to the place where they tried to kill him. Just like in Kenya: when they stoned us, brothers got hit in the jaw, and we went right back. We didn’t run. We ain’t going nowhere.
“To send chosen men unto you with our beloved Barnabas and Paul.” Barnabas and Paul had a team.

“Men that have hazarded their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.” Brothers, you are not here to be a professional student, just bringing a notebook on a Saturday, opening your Bible and hearing some breakdowns. The Bishop and Deacon Malachi say it all the time: your job is to learn this gospel, build your spirit up, go forth and teach.
Gamaliel, a Pharisee and doctor of the law, stands up in the council: “Ye men of Israel, take heed to yourselves what ye intend to do as touching these men.”

Theudas rose up “boasting himself to be somebody”, about four hundred men joined him, he was slain, “and all, as many as obeyed him, were scattered, and brought to nought.” His movement was brought to nothing.

Judas of Galilee “drew away much people after him: he also perished.” We have that today: brothers come to the body, learn the scriptures a little, go forth and heap men to themselves and scatter the men, and when they leave, the men come to nothing.

“Refrain from these men, and let them alone: for if this counsel or this work be of men, it will come to nought: But if it be of God, ye cannot overthrow it; lest haply ye be found even to fight against God.” Gamaliel tells them to leave these brothers alone. If what we are doing is of men, it will come to nothing; if it is of God, nobody can do anything about it. When they fight us, they are fighting God.

They beat the apostles and commanded them not to speak in the name of Jesus, “And they departed from the presence of the council, rejoicing that they were counted worthy to suffer shame for his name.” That is the level we have to get to: taking an ass whipping for the Lord and rejoicing over it, getting punched in the face and rejoicing over that, instead of wanting your lick back. That is a whole changing of the mind.
“And daily in the temple, and in every house, they ceased not to teach and preach Jesus Christ.” They didn’t try to get their lick back; they kept teaching.
“Stand up manfully, and I will advise thee.” This is where we have to get, brothers: how are we supposed to stand up? Manfully. And when we stand up manfully, the Lord is going to advise us.

“But without faith it is impossible to please him.” If you have faith, you cannot be bashful.

What is on the mind of a quiet, shy, timid brother? His mind is always on what other people are thinking, and you don’t know what he is thinking. When you are at war with brothers that are shy, timid and bashful, how are you going to trust that he won’t run on you, that he will defend you when a gun or a knife or an unruly mob comes out? You don’t know. It is a deceitful spirit: they hide in the cut. If you have faith you won’t be shy or timid, and brothers will know where you stand.

“For he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.”

“Above all, taking the shield of faith”: there is faith again. “Wherewith ye shall be able to quench all the fiery darts of the wicked.” If you ain’t got faith, you ain’t quenching any darts of the wicked; you will be taken away with the wicked.
“Let your yea be yea; and your nay, nay; lest ye fall into condemnation.”
“Is any among you afflicted? let him pray”: pray to the Lord.

“Is any sick among you? let him call for the elders of the church; and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord: And the prayer of faith shall save the sick, and the Lord shall raise him up; and if he have committed sins, they shall be forgiven him.” The prayer of what? The prayer of faith. There is faith again: it is the prayer of faith that saves the sick.

“Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed.” We ought to confess our faults one to another, and pray one for another. “The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much.”

This is when you go from a bashful sinner to a righteous man. “And the Spirit of the Lord will come upon thee”: you have the Holy Spirit, “and shalt be turned into another man.” You won’t be that bashful little boy in a man’s body anymore.
“And let it be, when these signs are come unto thee, that thou do as occasion serve thee; for God is with thee.” Brothers and sisters, you’ve got to believe that. Stop being bashful.
